title: Learned stromal expression score associates with colon-cancer outcomes
summary: A 31-gene score selected using elastic-net and penalized survival learning was associated with worse relapse-free and overall survival in retrospective colon-cancer data. A higher score also showed adverse-outcome associations in a separate TCGA cohort. The result is a clinical expression–outcome association, not proof of chemotherapy resistance or a treatment-selection benefit.
organization: Southern Medical University; Sun Yat-sen University

source_review.scope: Exact primary front and selected computational/clinical Methods and corresponding high-level Results; operational laboratory protocols excluded from review

evidence.tested: The score was developed using five GEO datasets totalling 990 cases and examined in 382 TCGA-COAD cases. Outcome-informed resampling and expression cutoffs selected genes; the final score subtracts the mean expression of negatively signed selected genes from the positive group. The source reports adjusted survival associations.
evidence.unknown: Prognostic outcomes inform development, selection and cutoffs; derivation-cohort associations are not independent validation. Treatment comparisons are observational and do not identify causal benefit or intrinsic resistance. Computational drug-response and pathway predictions are not measured clinical response. Supplemental implementation and treatment-confounding details were not inspected; separate experimental mechanisms are not represented.
evidence.ai_role: Elastic-net models learn stromal-group discriminators, and repeated penalized Cox fits select the expression features that constitute the measured-outcome-associated score.
